results.summary_before: This design implements an 8b10b decoder and a multiplier, intended as a test for a high-speed cell library. The decoder looks for the K.28.5 symbol to establish synchronization and then decodes subsequent data symbols. The multiplier operates on the decoded data. The design was tested at 200MHz and basic functionality was verified.
results.summary: This design implements an 8b10b decoder and a multiplier, intended as a test for a high-speed cell library. The decoder looks for the K.28.5 symbol to establish synchronization and then decodes subsequent data symbols. The multiplier operates on the decoded data. The author tested basic functionality with a modified cocotb script and verified decode and multiplier operation at a 200 MHz clock.

results.summary_before: This project simulates Conway's Game of Life using digital logic and outputs the cellular automaton patterns via VGA. The simulation runs automatically upon power-up, and can be paused or randomized via input pins. It requires a Tiny Tapeout VGA Pmod for display. The design is a hardware implementation of a classic cellular automaton, created as a summer project at SJSU.

results.summary_before: This design drives an external ADG732 32-channel multiplexer, cycling through output channels at 1 Hz to test multistrand cables. It divides a 10 MHz clock to 1 Hz and generates chip select and write signals for the multiplexer. Testing can be done with an FPGA (e.g., iCE40) or with the actual ADG732 chip on a custom PCB. The project originated as a cable assembly test tool.

results.summary_before: This is a 2.4 GHz integer-N PLL with an output divide-by-100, producing a frequency range of 19.2–25.2 MHz. It uses a 20 MHz reference clock and allows digital control of the divider factor and VCO discrete tuning to overcome process variation. Outputs include an analog pin (FOUT) and two digital pins, with an analog control voltage pin (VCON) for observation. The design is analog and requires an external 20 MHz clock.
